refutation_attempt: Read all 16 TransformWindowToLogical overrides, RegisterForWindow callers, Mouse/bridge fallbacks, docs and tests. Raw fallback is real, but Overscan's rectangle covers the whole window so it never declines; GDI (registered, declines) is a seventh renderer; nothing pins bar behaviour.
reason: Real: window_to_logical and to_logical_position keep the raw coordinate when a renderer returns false, so a Letterbox-bar pointer reads as an in-playfield position; the fidelity doc's premise that bars carry no game position is contradicted. Scope is wrong: only Letterbox has bars (not Overscan) and GDI also declines.

correction.summary: EasyGL (every GL-family identity), OPENGL4, SDL_GPU, WEBGPU, SVG_DOM, HTML_DOM and GDI decline points outside the presented rectangle, and Mouse and the input bridge then report the untransformed window coordinate, which can look like a valid game position. This happens only where the presented rectangle is smaller than the window, that is under CnaPresentationMode::Letterbox (or for a pointer outside the window); Overscan, Stretch, NativeBackBuffer and the default FixedHeightDynamicWidth present a rectangle that covers the whole window.
correction.actual: WindowToLogical in modules/graphics/include/CNA/Internal/Renderers/Common/GlPresentationSurfaceState.hpp (EasyGL, OPENGL4) computes the logical coordinates and then returns windowX >= clientViewportX && ..., i.e. false inside a Letterbox bar; SDL_GPU, WebGPU, SVG_DOM, HTML_DOM and GDI (MapGdiWindowToLogical) do the same. On false, window_to_logical in modules/input/src/Xna/Mouse.cpp leaves the output at the raw window coordinate, and to_logical_position in modules/input/src/Internal/SdlInputBridge.cpp returns it too. With a 100-pixel left bar, a pointer at window x = 50 is reported as game x = 50, inside the playfield. Under Overscan the presented rectangle extends past every window edge, so in-window points always map.
correction.evidence_note: Read every TransformWindowToLogical override and every RegisterForWindow call at 009d40f5; not executed. DIRECTX11, DIRECTX12 and METAL also decline outside the rectangle but never register for their window (CNA-BUG-133), so input never consults them; VULKAN, Canvas, Direct2D, FNA3D, the SDL renderer and FREEDIRECT return true without a range check.

refutation_attempt: Looked for a capability check or catch in the wrappers, callers that handle the throw, and a headless/Terminal null-mouse path. Wrappers call the mouse directly; Wayland and Terminal always throw; only headless (GetMouse null) is safe. PLAT-013 explicitly defers the escape to this entry.
reason: Mouse.hpp documents false for unsupported platforms and GetGlobalPositionEXT zeroes first, yet WaylandMouse and TerminalMouse throw PlatformNotSupportedException from all three methods and the wrappers neither check GlobalPointer nor catch. The C API wrappers sit behind an exception barrier; C++ callers see the throw. Low severity fits.

refutation_attempt: Searched CNA docs and tests for the ISO key and VolumeMute. docs/input-fna-fidelity.md records dropping NonUsBackslash as accepted INPUT-KBD-011/019 (CNA does not invent a divergent OemBackslash), and UnknownAndIsoExtraScancodesAreDropped asserts it. The entry's claim that no test asserts it is wrong.
reason: The unmapped ISO scancodes and the VolumeMute omission are a documented, tested, FNA-parity decision, and Keyboard.hpp documents an empty name for keys without a scancode. XNA has no scancode API, so no XNA contract is violated; only the xkb keycode path knowing OemBackslash is a design difference, not a defect.
read: docs/input-fna-fidelity.md::Keyboard intentional deviations INPUT-KBD-011/019 and unmapped media keys

refutation_attempt: Looked for an OFF-aware resync, a per-track guard or a documented limitation. SDL3's diagnosticAlive only prevents double decrements; only EndMixerEngineShutdown resets; docs list only the resource limitation; no engine code lowers the mode, so an application must. Re-derived drift by reading AddMetric.
reason: AddMetric returns while the runtime mode is OFF, both mixer backends keep Audio/AllocatedVoices with +1/-1 deltas (default Accuracy::Exact), so a create or destroy inside an OFF window leaves it wrong until shutdown. Undocumented against 'gauges retain the latest value' and 'exact'. The recorded g++ run was not repeated here.
read: docs/diagnostics.md::Build and runtime modes; Known limitations; built-in engine metrics

refutation_attempt: Checked whether the frame is closed elsewhere or spans successive callbacks: FrameScope measures scope duration only, the rAF await sits in RunLoop after the callback returns, the accumulator never waits. Compared with BUG-080 (clock/exception contract): different defect. Inspector is not built for web, as claimed.
reason: Native Game::Tick opens the frame scope around the pacing waits, while EmscriptenMainLoopCallback holds it and RunLoop awaits requestAnimationFrame outside, so web durationNs and framesPerSecond (1e9/duration) report work rate. docs/diagnostics.md gives one frame definition for both loops. Narrow diagnostics effect, low severity is right.

refutation_attempt: Checked whether the hello uses a runtime accessor, whether getCurrentGraphicsRendererType is really compile-time in multi-renderer builds, and whether CNA documents the compile-time answer as intended. It is constexpr from the default CNA_RENDERER_* macro; GraphicsDevice.hpp itself says a compile-time answer cannot describe a runtime choice.
reason: Agent::Impl::HandleClient sets hello.graphicsRenderer from the compile-time default, while GraphicsRendererSelection::GetActive and GraphicsDevice::GetGraphicsRendererName exist for the runtime choice; a preference, environment variable or fallback in a multi-renderer build makes the Session view wrong. Single-renderer builds are unaffected; low severity fits.

refutation_attempt: Looked for per-item truncation or filtering in HandleSnapshot/HandleEvents, a bound in CopyResource, and docs making whole-response refusal intended. None filter; docs say only oversized snapshots are refused and state no name bound. Re-derived the 1 MiB versus 4,096 mismatch by reading.
reason: RegisterMetric and RegisterName accept names up to 1 MiB and CopyResource bounds nothing, but Protocol.cpp Writer::String throws length_error above 4,096 bytes for metric, resource and event names, and HandleRequest turns it into LimitExceeded for the whole request. Metrics are never unregistered. Trigger needs unusual application names, so low is right.

refutation_attempt: Traced Stop against Run: the missed shutdown is real, no stopping_ check follows accept, and header and payload get separate 3 s deadlines. But the window is wider than claimed: the accept poll returns on any connection during the 200 ms after Stop sets stopping_.
reason: Real bounded delay (about 3 s for a silent peer, up to about 6 s if a header arrives without its payload). Correction: the trigger is not only a connection accepted before Stop's shutdown step, but any connection the still-polling worker accepts during the following accept interval of up to 200 ms.

correction.title: Agent::Stop can wait up to about six seconds for a connection that the accept loop takes around the time Stop runs
correction.summary: Stop shuts down only a client already published as activeClient_, and the worker never re-checks stopping_ after accepting. A connection accepted just before Stop, or during the accept poll of up to 200 ms that follows Stop setting stopping_, is therefore never shut down, and join waits on that client's handshake reads, up to 3 s for the header and 3 s for the payload.
correction.actual: Agent::Impl::Run publishes an accepted socket as activeClient_ (under socketMutex_) only after AcceptTcp returns, and HandleClient starts the handshake without re-checking stopping_. Stop sets stopping_, shuts down whatever activeClient_ holds at that moment (InvalidSocket when nothing is published) and joins. The worker only notices stopping_ when its 200 ms accept poll times out, and the poll returns at once when a connection arrives, so a connection accepted just before Stop or at any point in that interval is published after Stop's shutdown step and served anyway. HandleClient then blocks in ReceivePacket, which applies HandshakeTimeoutMilliseconds (3,000) to the 24-byte header and again to the payload. A client that sends a valid ClientHello at once ends the wait early; a silent local peer holds Stop, and therefore a game's ~Agent, for about 3 s, and one that sends a complete header and withholds the payload for up to about 6 s.
correction.evidence_note: Checked by reading modules/inspector/src/Agent.cpp and modules/inspector/src/InternalSocket.cpp at 009d40f5. Not executed; the window follows from the 200 ms accept poll and is not measured.

refutation_attempt: Traced the owner token from cna_graphics_device_create through CreateOwnedTexture2D and the index buffer to the route; checked HandleRegistry::Get kind mismatch, whether dispose nulls the resource's device pointer, and docs or tests for this case. Route calls GetGame on an OwnedGraphicsDevice handle; nothing documents it.
reason: The owner token of a caller-created device is its own handle, copied into every resource, yet cna_graphics_resource_get_graphics_device passes it to the game-only BorrowGameGraphicsDevice, so HandleRegistry::Get answers CNA_RESULT_INVALID_HANDLE for valid resources, alive or destroyed device. CABI-13 said no route needed to know about owned devices; this site was missed.

refutation_attempt: Tested whether 'producer thread' could just mean the creation thread. The C++ class documents producer-thread-callable entry points and the C source comment says the copy lets a producer thread reuse its buffer, yet Get returns CNA_RESULT_THREAD off-thread; LIMITATIONS.md states thread affinity globally.
reason: audio.h and AUDIO.md's streaming paragraph present cross-thread submission as canonical usage, but both submit routes resolve the instance through HandleRegistry::Get, which refuses any other thread, and AUDIO.md's own threading section says every audio call runs on the creation thread. Contract text is inconsistent with behaviour; low because failure is a clean error code.

refutation_attempt: Grepped the whole tree, tests included, for CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN and any registry or game shutdown flag that could produce it. Only abi.h, the ABI baseline, docs and the ErrorCategoryForResult mapping mention it; game shutdown and stale handles yield INVALID_HANDLE or INVALID_STATE. Not marked reserved anywhere.
reason: HANDLES.md's validation table (and ERRORS.md and abi.h) promise CNA_RESULT_SHUTTING_DOWN when the runtime is closing or closed, but no route returns it, the registry keeps no such state, and stale handles answer INVALID_HANDLE. A documented result code that cannot occur misleads bindings that branch on it; low is right.

refutation_attempt: Searched the whole tree for IDiagnosticsSource, RegisterSource and AudioVoice, including tests, examples and unrelated shader hits. Confirmed no production source or voice registration; docs call the GPU seam future. But no test references ResourceKind::AudioVoice, contrary to the entry.
reason: Real gap, documented as a seam: no engine code implements IDiagnosticsSource or registers AudioVoice metadata, so those views stay empty. Correction: AudioVoice appears only in the enum, the Inspector bridge name table and the web UI's Audio filter; no test references it, and the source seam is tested only with test sources.

correction.actual: A search of modules/ finds IDiagnosticsSource and RegisterSource implemented and used only in the diagnostics module and its tests. ResourceKind::AudioVoice appears only in its enum definition, the Inspector bridge's name table (ResourceKindName) and the web UI's Audio view filter; no engine code registers such a resource and no test references it. The audio module publishes the Audio/AllocatedVoices gauge and the Audio/VoiceCreations counter but registers no voice resources, so the Inspector Audio view's list of registered audio resources is always empty. docs/diagnostics.md documents the GPU part ("GPU timings are an extension seam only; no renderer publishes them yet").

refutation_attempt: Searched the tree for implementers or installers of IResourcePreviewProvider and every pendingPreviews_ use for a provider notification on disconnect or failure. Only Agent.hpp, its tests, benchmark and docs mention it; Run merely clears the map; the interface has two methods and no bound-outstanding statement.
reason: No CNA renderer or example installs a preview provider, so ResourcePreviews is never negotiated, as docs/inspector.md records. The seam has no cancel or expiry hook: the agent clears pending tickets on disconnect without telling the provider, and a reconnecting client can start up to 4 (max 16) more. A documented deferral plus an undocumented seam limit; a gap fits.
